scoreRule: One point per correct answer; ten points maximum. Provisional local result only.
description: Original ten-question B1 English Reading assessment draft; teacher content audit is still required.

tabs.title: Understanding
tabs.description: Understand the central ideas and the people.

tabs.title: Using What You Read
tabs.description: Apply the idea in a new situation.

questions.q: What did the writer want to demonstrate when he accepted the challenge?
choices: That phone calls were forbidden at school.
That everyone in his class spent too little time online.
That living without chat apps would not be difficult for him.
That email was always more popular than messages.
questions.explanation: The diary contrasts the speed of calls with the coordination benefits of group messages and ends by choosing more mindful communication.

questions.q: What did checking an empty phone many times reveal to the writer?
choices: His phone was not working properly that morning.
He was used to looking for new messages even when there were none.
The teacher had secretly turned off the school internet.
His classmates had stopped sending messages to one another.
questions.explanation: The diary contrasts the speed of calls with the coordination benefits of group messages and ends by choosing more mindful communication.

questions.q: Why did Karim initially react with concern to the call?
choices: The writer had forgotten to invite Karim to football.
The coach asked Karim to change the training time.
Karim was waiting for a message from his grandparents.
He was not used to his friend phoning him unexpectedly.
questions.explanation: The diary contrasts the speed of calls with the coordination benefits of group messages and ends by choosing more mindful communication.

questions.q: Why could a quick phone call be more efficient than the group chat?
choices: It answered a specific question without a long discussion.
It was the only way to use the internet on the bus.
It allowed the writer to change all his friends' plans.
It stopped anyone else from attending football training.
questions.explanation: The diary contrasts the speed of calls with the coordination benefits of group messages and ends by choosing more mindful communication.

questions.q: What did the missed history meeting show about the challenge?
choices: His friends did not want him to work on the presentation.
The library had been permanently closed that morning.
Not using group messages could leave him without important updates.
He had forgotten the correct date of the school project.
questions.explanation: The diary contrasts the speed of calls with the coordination benefits of group messages and ends by choosing more mindful communication.

questions.q: Why did the writer feel 'like a tourist in my own class'?
choices: He missed a shared experience that everyone else could discuss.
He had started studying at a different school.
The history presentation was about tourism.
His classmates were speaking a language he could not understand.
questions.explanation: The diary contrasts the speed of calls with the coordination benefits of group messages and ends by choosing more mindful communication.

questions.q: What does the writer's new use of notifications suggest?
choices: He has decided never to use a phone again.
He now chooses which messages need his attention.
He reads every group message as soon as it arrives.
He uses only email for all communication.
questions.explanation: The diary contrasts the speed of calls with the coordination benefits of group messages and ends by choosing more mindful communication.

questions.q: You need a quick answer about tomorrow's training. What option follows the writer's experience?
choices: Wait for a long chat even if it gives no clear answer.
Avoid finding out because the question is not important.
Send the same question to everyone twenty times.
A brief call can be useful when messages are slow or confusing.
questions.explanation: The diary contrasts the speed of calls with the coordination benefits of group messages and ends by choosing more mindful communication.

questions.q: A class project changes its meeting location. What would help a pupil who cannot access the group chat?
choices: Assume that every meeting will always be held in the same room.
Agree on another reliable way to receive important changes.
Stop going to all meetings until the week is over.
Ask the teacher to cancel the project.
questions.explanation: The diary contrasts the speed of calls with the coordination benefits of group messages and ends by choosing more mindful communication.

questions.q: Which conclusion best matches the writer's final attitude to messaging?
choices: All chat apps should be banned because they always waste time.
Communication was easier in every situation without them.
A week away from messaging proved that phones cannot help friendships.
The apps can be useful, but he can make more deliberate choices about using them.
questions.explanation: The diary contrasts the speed of calls with the coordination benefits of group messages and ends by choosing more mindful communication.
